newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ takes novel approach to Gulf Arab cheese market.
newsitem.headline: NZ takes novel approach to Gulf Arab cheese market.

text.p: New Zealand's Dairy Board is breaking into the competitive Gulf Arab market for processed cheese by injecting the foodstuff into plastic packs moulded in the shape of toys.
A spokesman told Reuters on Thursday the move was based on research that indicated "the influence young people in the region have on what their parents put into the trolley".
The age-oriented strategy is showing early success, he added, with demand for the "Cheez Toyz" outstripping production just three weeks after launch in the Saudi Arabian market.
"Our objective has been to come over the top of the market to leapfrog the competitors, and to do that we needed to innovate," spokesman Neville Martin said.
The brightly-coloured packs come in eight different plastic toy shapes, including rockets, robots and teddy bears, so children can peel and eat the cheese then keep the toy.
A Dairy Board plant in Damman, Saudi Arabia, is churning out the toys under the Chesdale brand. They contain processed cheese made locally with raw materials from New Zealand.
Martin said the company was aiming for a substantial share of a regional processed cheese market the board estimates to be worth US$150 million, but he declined to specify a target.
Leading competitors are European products including the triangular-packaged Laughing Cow brand of France's La Vache Qui Rit (The Laughing Cow), and the red roundel of Baby Bel.
New product sales were already on track to reach the board's target of 50 tonnes a month, Martin noted.
Once the line is established in Saudi Arabia the board may try selling it in neighbouring markets such as Qatar, Yemen, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, and the United Arab Emirates.
